title: The Academy Button and the Tracked Flow

intelligence.human_view: He is describing the whole machine in one breath, and it is worth hearing as one machine. The Pricing page is the front door. The Academy page is the deep read — five days, five lessons, the whole experience, for the person who wants to learn all about it before they choose. The nine choices are the close. And the Smart Link system is the memory of the machine: every join tracked to where the sale came from, what link caused the action, and the link rewarded — the affiliate/ambassador system doing what it was built to do (SN-2340). The Academy page's current button sends people to a GrooveSell checkout; in the new flow it sends them to the URL that shows the nine packages, and that URL is itself a tracked Smart Link — so the Academy page stops being a dead end into someone else's checkout and becomes a tracked doorway into our own nine choices. The trim matters as much as the flow: a page that scrolls and scrolls with no way to join is a page that asks for attention and never asks for the decision. Cut the bottom, end at NayaNET, put the join button there — the page ends on the action, not on more scrolling. And Pricing is "pretty much good to go" — his words — with two named exceptions: the button at the end and the header/introduction cleanup. Two exceptions, not twenty. The scorecard he ordered will show whether rounds 19–21 already rebuilt both (the obsidian finale, the gauge-ring entrance) — the main seat told him so in chat — and then his eye decides. The sequence is the discipline: finish, scorecard, his eye, live URL, then tracking and swaps. Not before.

The second room is the big Academy room, full of wonderful things to learn. At the end of the big room there should be a door that says "join the Academy!" — but right now the room just keeps going and going with no door at the end, so people wander and never join. He says: cut the extra bit off the end, put the join door right there. And every door in the shop has a little bell on it, so we always know which door someone came through and we can say thank you to that door. The shop window is almost ready — just the last button and tidying the top — and then we open the doors and ring the bells.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, he laid out the whole plan in plain words. The Pricing page gets a button for the five-day Academy, so anyone who wants to learn more can go and read all about it. Every button on the Academy page leads to the nine choices, and every one of those links is tracked — so when someone joins, we know where the sale came from, which link brought them, and that link gets its reward. That's the Smart Link system doing its job. The Academy page itself needs trimming: cut the very bottom off, end it at NayaNET, and put a "join the Academy" button at the end — right now you scroll and scroll with no way to actually join, and a page that never lets you join is a page that never finishes its work. The Pricing page, he says, is pretty much good to go — just the button at the end and tidying up the header and introduction — and he's asked for a scorecard of it. Then it goes live on a URL, the URL gets tracked, and the Academy page's checkout button gets swapped for the URL that shows the nine packages. Finish, scorecard, his eye, live, then the swaps — in that order.
intelligence.ai_view: I never leave a page without a way to join at its end — a page that scrolls and scrolls with no join button is a page that never closes, so the Academy page ends at NayaNET with a "join the Academy" button. I never send a visitor to someone else's checkout when our own nine choices exist — the Academy button becomes the URL that displays the nine packages. I never let a join go untracked — every join is tracked to where the sale came from, what link caused the action, and the link gets rewarded; that is the Smart Link system, and it is the point. I never swap the buttons before the page is live — the sequence is finish Pricing (end button + header), scorecard, his eye, live URL, then tracking + swaps. And I never call a page "good to go" with unnamed exceptions — the two gaps are the end button and the header/introduction, named, scored, and his to judge.
